item.title: "48 Hours" show schedule
item.description: True crime. Real justice. To miss it would be a crime.

item.title: Was Sylvie Cachay's death at Soho House an accident or murder?
item.description: An Oscar winner’s son is accused of killing his swimsuit designer girlfriend at a trendy NYC hotel.

item.title: Death at Soho House
item.description: An Oscar winner's son, a fashion designer girlfriend -- one is dead. Was it murder? "48 Hours" correspondent Troy Roberts investigates.

item.title: Rare clue at Minneapolis crime scene points to a barefoot killer
item.description: "In Minnesota here, people are not committing crimes a lot of times with the socks and shoes off," said a forensic scientist about footprints left in the victim's blood.

item.title: Bloody, bare footprints lead to decadeslong search for woman's killer
item.description: In 1993, Jeanie Childs was found stabbed more than 60 times in her Minneapolis apartment. Bloody footprints and unknown DNA left investigators without answers until a 2015 cold-case review and public DNA database finally pointed to a suspect.

item.title: Several people killed in shooting at Idaho In-N-Out restaurant, officials say
item.description: Several people were killed in a shooting Saturday afternoon at an In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls, Idaho, local authorities said.

item.title: Several people killed in explosion at Moscow restaurant, Russian officials say
item.description: An explosion Saturday at a Moscow restaurant that killed three people and wounded 21 others was a bombing, Russian authorities said.

item.title: Trump says attack on Iran canceled after rough framework of deal reached
item.description: President Trump announced Saturday night that he will cancel a pending attack on Iran after he indicated that a rough framework of a peace deal had been reached.

item.title: Trump says deal to end Iran war may be imminent, agrees to "cancel the attack"
item.description: On Saturday, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke with Mr. Trump and cautioned him against conducting a fresh round of strikes on Iran, CBS News learned.

item.title: The Footprint
item.description: A woman is murdered in her home and the pivotal clue at the crime is a bloody footprint her killer left behind. "48 Hours" correspondent Erin Moriarty reports.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning": The Money Issue (Aug. 2)
item.description: This week Jane Pauley hosts "The Money Issue," our annual special broadcast dedicated to the many ways in which money underscores the way we live.

item.title: World's largest locomotive, Union Pacific's Big Boy, completes epic journey
item.description: Ian Lee traces this summer's cross-country journey of the world's largest locomotive, known as Big Boy.

item.title: Investigating the death of designer Sylvie Cachay
item.description: Sylvie Cachay was found dead in an overflowing bathtub at the exclusive Soho House in New York City on Dec. 9, 2010. A water leak at the hotel gave away a timeline that may have revealed her killer.

item.title: France makes major progress in wildfire fight, but danger still lurks
item.description: Even though France's biggest wildfire crisis since 1949 has been contained, many of the blazes are still burning. Ramy Inocencio reports from France.

item.title: FIFA reverses course on World Cup private investment plan
item.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino announced Friday that he is canceling a proposal that would have seen the world soccer governing body sell private shares in the World Cup. His reversal came after the plan drew heavy criticism from member nations.

item.title: Hollywood's summer blockbuster season is experiencing a renaissance
item.description: The summer blockbuster may be having its own blockbuster comeback. After years of streaming dominance, audiences are again packing theaters. Adam Yamaguchi has more.

item.title: Oil companies see soaring profits amid Iran war
item.description: As the threat of escalation in the war with Iran drives gas prices higher and hurts economies worldwide, one sector is doing really well, the revenue for Big Oil. Ali Bauman explains.

item.title: Tensions rise in Iran war with threat of new strikes
item.description: There was a sense that the war with Iran could potentially enter a more dangerous phase, with sources telling CBS News that the U.S. and Israel were preparing for what could be the most aggressive expansion of the campaign against Iran since the war began. Imtiaz Tyab reports.

item.title: DOJ to dismiss Reflecting Pool vandalism charges, citing "botched installation"
item.description: Federal prosecutors moved to dismiss an indictment charging U.S. Olympic canoeist David Hearn with ripping the bottom of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, saying the damage was caused by "botched installation and not vandalism."

item.title: Vincent Pastore, famous for his role in "The Sopranos," dies at 80
item.description: Vincent Pastore played Salvatore "Big Pussy" Bonpensiero on all six seasons of "The Sopranos," which aired from 1999 to 2007.

item.title: Trump blasts Pirro's decision to drop charges in Reflecting Pool case
item.description: President Trump on Saturday took issue with U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro's decision to dismiss charges against former U.S. Olympic canoeist David Hearn, who was accused of vandalizing the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. However, Pirro found that peeled paint was actually caused by "flawed installation by the contractor," and she instead placed blame on the Interior Department. Olivia Rinaldi has the latest.

item.title: Actor Vincent Pastore, best known for "The Sopranos," dies at 80
item.description: Actor Vincent Pastore, who was best known for his role in the acclaimed series "The Sopranos," has died at the age of 80.

item.title: 8/1: CBS Weekend News
item.description: President Trump criticizes decision to drop charges in Reflecting Pool case; Tensions rise in the Middle East.

item.title: 10 climbers, including famed mountaineer, dead in Pakistan avalanche
item.description: The 10-person expedition lost contact with its base camp after an avalanche struck Broad Peak as they attempted to scale the mountain.

item.title: Wildfire danger in Europe shifts to Greece as evacuation orders remain in France
item.description: For Greece, the danger carried grim resonance: a 2018 wildfire​ at the seaside community of Mati​, near Athens, killed 104 people.

item.title: Bombing in Colombia injures 11, days before presidential inauguration
item.description: President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella condemned the bombing and said "terrorism will not intimidate Colombia."

item.title: Trump will push for "anti-weaponization fund" if Blanche not confirmed, he says
item.description: Todd Blanche previously repeatedly told Congress the "anti-weaponization fund" was "dead."

item.title: UEFA says it has lost confidence in FIFA leadership after investment plan
item.description: FIFA chief Gianni Infantino had proposed creating a $20 billion company to run the World Cup with private investors but drew backlash that grew every day since Tuesday's announcement.

item.title: A brief timeline of Iranian cyberattacks on the U.S.
item.description: Investigators are probing whether Iranian hackers are behind this week's malicious cyber activity against water systems in Minnesota. If they are found to be the culprits, it would not be the first time.

item.title: Survivor's testimony key in helping convict ex-boyfriend of murder
item.description: C.C. Opanowski says it's still difficult to process the fact that a person she once loved was convicted of murder. She hopes that others can learn from her story.
